original_value: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, how to take advantage of deep learning and big data to classify polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery is a hot topic in the field of remote sensing. As a key step for PolSAR image classification, feature extraction technology based on target decomposition is relatively mature, and how to extract discriminative spatial features and integrate these features with polarized information to maximize the classification accuracy is the core issue. In this context, this paper proposes a PolSAR image classification algorithm based on fully convolutional networks (FCNs) and a manifold graph embedding model. First, to describe different types of land objects more comprehensively, various polarized features of PolSAR images are extracted through seven kinds of traditional decomposition methods. Afterwards, drawing on transfer learning, the decomposed features are fed into multiple parallel and pre-trained FCN-8s models to learn deep multi-scale spatial features. Feature maps from the last layer of each FCN model are concatenated to obtain spatial polarization features with high dimensions. Then, a manifold graph embedding model is adopted to seek an effective and compact representation for spatially polarized features in a manifold subspace, simultaneously removing redundant information. Finally, a support vector machine (SVM) is selected as the classifier for pixel-level classification in a manifold subspace. Extensive experiments on three PolSAR datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves a superior classification performance.

result.paraphrase: With the rapid progress of artificial intelligence, using deep learning and big data to classify polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery has become a hot topic in remote sensing. As an essential step in PolSAR image classification, target-decomposition-based feature extraction is relatively mature; the central challenge is how to extract discriminative spatial features and fuse them with polarization information to achieve the highest possible classification accuracy. Against this backdrop, this paper presents a PolSAR image classification method that combines fully convolutional networks (FCNs) with a manifold graph embedding model. First, to more fully characterize different land-cover types, polarized features are extracted from PolSAR images using seven traditional decomposition methods. Next, inspired by transfer learning, the decomposed features are input into multiple parallel pre-trained FCN-8s models to learn deep multi-scale spatial features. The feature maps from the final layer of each FCN are concatenated to form high-dimensional spatial-polarization features. A manifold graph embedding model is then used to obtain an effective and compact representation of these features in a manifold subspace while eliminating redundant information. Finally, an SVM is employed as the classifier for pixel-level classification in the manifold subspace. Extensive experiments on three PolSAR datasets show that the proposed algorithm delivers superior classification performance.
